conviction_note: The Q2 core run rate ($0.59 with no provision, plus about $0.01-0.03 from the $40M sub-debt redemption on July 1) sits a little above the $0.57 bar. That is offset by a liability-sensitive balance sheet heading into a Sept 16 Fed hike, with about $600M of CDs repricing in Q3. The $19.8M OREO construction asset could break either way. Q2's $0.05 beat bought -0.41%, so p_up is only 55 on an abs move of 3.0 (the 7-print mean |move| is 2.75 and there is no usable chain), which gives +0.3. The findings sum to +0.55, and they are not fitted to that number.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $0.57 (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/RBB; Tickflow https://www.tickflow.io/stock/RBB/forecast shows the same $0.57 and ~$34M revenue). A Nasdaq/Zacks page of unclear date shows $0.53 / $33.06M (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/rbb-rbb-earnings-expected-grow-should-you-buy). Two sources agree, one older source disagrees, and there is no company guidance. Q2 actual was $0.59 against a $0.54 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest was 463.8K shares on the Aug 20, 2026 settlement, up 60.6K, with 2.3 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/rbb/shortinterest). That is about 2.7% of 16.9M shares outstanding, so the short is not crowded. No October figure was found. The baseline options chain is empty, so there is no skew. Unusual Whales quotes about 5.66% implied (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/RBB/earnings), which could not be verified against the sealed chain. Run-up is +0.06% over 5 days and -3.91% over 20 days. The stock is 7.9% below its 52-week high, at about 0.94x Q2 TBV of $27.23.

findings.finding: On July 1, 2026 RBB redeemed $40.0M of its $120M sub notes, which had repriced on April 1 from a fixed 4.00% to a floating 6.98% (the remaining $80M resets at 7.02%). That removes about $0.70M a quarter of interest expense. Net of roughly $0.4M of lost yield on the ~$40.7M of cash used, it is about +$0.3-0.7M pre-tax, or +$0.01-0.03 EPS, against a $0.57 bar that sits below Q2's $0.59.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's NIM fell 9bp on the sub-debt repricing, and the stock moved -0.41% on a $0.05 EPS beat (baseline 2026-07-20). No print has yet shown the saving.
findings.why_not_priced: The redemption was disclosed, but the company gave no savings figure, and the consensus ($0.57) sits below the Q2 run rate. If analysts had modelled the saving, the consensus would be at or above $0.59-0.60.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript, where Johnny Lee says the redemption will 'reduce interest expense in future quarters' (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026). It comes from the same company, so it is not independent of the release.

findings.finding: The $0.57 consensus sits below Q2's $0.59, and Q2 itself was clean. It carried no provision and an OREO loss of -$221K rather than a gain, and none of Q1's one-offs ($890K OREO gain, $484K recovery, $360K tax-refund interest, $430K FHLB special dividend). Management guided to mid-to-high single-digit annualised loan growth in H2 (Q2 originations $159M at 6.31%) and deposit costs 'relatively the same or slightly improved'. So the bar is a modest one, which the company beat by $0.05 last quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: $0.59 against $0.54 moved -0.41%. Q1 2026 ($0.66) moved +5.45%. Q3 2025 moved +6.76%. Five of seven prints were up, so beats were paid inconsistently.
findings.why_not_priced: Thin coverage (about 5 analysts, ~$2M a day of turnover) and a consensus below the Q2 print suggest the estimates bake in a provision or OREO loss. If the market expected a beat, the stock would not be 4% down over 20 days at 0.94x TBV.
findings.independence: The Q2 release itself, a primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926023874/ex_970512.htm), which shares a company source with finding 1. The bar source is https://www.tickflow.io/stock/RBB/forecast.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16, 2026, after management had flagged 'higher for longer'. RBB described itself as liability-sensitive: a 98% loan-to-deposit ratio, market deposit pricing near 4% against about $600M (roughly 40% of $1.5B) of CDs maturing or repricing in Q3 at about 3.70%, and $80M of floating sub notes. Peer FB Financial printed Q3 NIM down 12bp on rising deposit costs. That risks NIM compression in Q3 and a weaker Q4 margin outlook on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 NIM fell 9bp, the EPS beat anyway, and the stock moved -0.41%. The margin line has had no clean isolated test.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, but its pass-through to this name's CD book is not modelled in a $0.57 consensus that still implies flat-to-up revenue ($34M against $33.1M in Q2). If the market had priced the margin squeeze, revenue estimates would be flat or down.
findings.independence: Proxy only: FB Financial's Q3 NIM was down 12bp with deposit costs up (https://briefglance.com/articles/fb-financial-surges-in-q3-organic-growth-masks-margin-squeeze, 2026-10-13). Regions' Q3 NIM was up, which points the other way (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026). The company itself has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: The largest problem asset, a $19.4M partially completed construction credit, moved to OREO in Q2 (OREO $19.8M). Management targeted 'a resolution in the second half of this year' and said the carrying value is supported by a recent as-is appraisal, though it still needs 'the right buyer'. A Q3 sale would cut NPAs (Q2 $43.6M, 1.02% of assets) by nearly half. A write-down or a further delay is the other side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 NPAs fell 10.8% (NPLs -47% on the OREO transfer), and the stock moved -0.41%. The credit cleanup has not been rewarded in isolation.
findings.why_not_priced: The outcome is unknowable before the release. A credit-cleanup rerating would show as a move toward or above TBV ($27.23), and the stock is at $25.7.
findings.independence: The Q2 release reports OREO rising to $19.8M from $4.3M and NPAs at $43.6M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926023874/ex_970512.htm). That is the same company, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Capital return: a new plan for up to 1M shares (about 6% of the 16.9M outstanding) runs through June 2028, and 180,576 shares were bought back in Q2 at about $24.65. Management called its buyback appetite 'healthy' with the stock 'right around' tangible book, and said a dividend increase is 'something we would consider'. Q3 traded at $25-27, at or below TBV, so the buyback is TBV-accretive, with a possible dividend raise from the current $0.16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The plan was announced June 15 with the Q2 print, and that print moved -0.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 buyback volume and any dividend change are unknown until the release. A dividend raise would be news, since the consensus forward dividend is $0.64.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026), which is the same company.

findings.finding: An 8-K (item 5.02) dated Sept 8 says EVP and Chief Operations Officer Gary Fan leaves Sept 30, 2026 by 'mutual decision' as 'part of the Bank's leadership transition plan'. He receives six months' salary as severance, and no successor is named. That means a small Q3 severance cost and an open question on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: A quiet 8-K that no wire covered. If it signalled trouble, the price would have reacted in September, and the stock sat near $26.

findings.finding: Expense guide: management said the expense base should stay in the $18-19M range and is 'probably at the higher end' (Q2 was $19.0M), with continued hiring for the new Northern California team (Burlington LPO). Expenses are therefore flat at best, inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated expense surprise in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the stated guide, so it is largely priced.
findings.independence: This shares the transcript with findings 2, 4 and 5 (different statements).

findings.finding: Sell-side stance: Hovde upgraded to Outperform with a $29 target on June 16, 2026, and Stephens raised its target to $29 from $26 (Equal Weight) on July 23, 2026. The average target is about $28.50, roughly 11% above the $25.70 spot.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire information and is mostly priced. Filed only for completeness.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Higher Treasury yields and wider MBS spreads in Q3 2026 hurting AOCI and TBV
rejected_candidates.detail: Only a passing mention in a Dynex item on a dynamic MarketBeat page. There is no dated, stable source for the Q3 yield move or for RBB's AFS duration.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q3 figures surfaced by AAII/Nasdaq ($0.59 against $0.54) and by Cathay ($77.7M)
rejected_candidates.detail: The AAII item is the Q2 2026 print mislabelled as Q3, and the Cathay figure is Q3 2025. Both are contradicted by the Q2 8-K and by Cathay's 2025 release.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slightly positive lean (a run rate above the bar, at 0.94x TBV) runs against the -3.9% 20-day drift, and a macro rate-hike headwind partly offsets it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6/core: the sub-debt saving lands inside what the company already disclosed, so it was trimmed from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lessons 1 and 6: the bar is sourced twice but a third source disagrees ($0.53), and the last beat bought -0.41%, so the bar finding was trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 5: the Fed-hike and peer-NIM transmission is a proxy, so it was kept and trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4.
The expense item sits inside the guide, so it moved toward 0 (-0.1 to -0.05).
